rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate the elution window for all 10 compounds and identify critical pairs while minimizing truncation risk. Midrange temperature leaves room to explore temperature-dependent selectivity in either direction.

Halve the gradient duration to reduce the time penalty while testing how the critical pairs respond to slope. The initial minimum resolution of 2.36 provides room to accelerate without immediately sacrificing separation.

Use an intermediate gradient duration to recover resolution in the slope-sensitive central cluster while retaining most of the time savings. This brackets the shortest gradient that may achieve the full resolution term.

Raise temperature while keeping the gradient fixed to test selectivity of the remaining critical pair. Faster elution should preserve the zero time penalty, and a modest selectivity shift may lift its resolution above 1.5.

The central-cluster pattern suggests that the critical pair crossed between 40 and 50 C; another 5 C may separate it enough to reach full resolution. Keep the gradient unchanged to isolate this selectivity effect while maintaining a zero time penalty.

Slightly increase gradient slope from 0.0643 to 0.0667 organic fraction per minute to try to lift the critical pair above 1.5 while preserving the neighboring pair's margin. The final organic fraction remains comfortably above the observed elution window, and the time penalty should remain zero.

Increase the slope slightly again to push the remaining critical pair toward resolution 1.5, while the neighboring pair should retain sufficient separation. All compounds should still elute with zero time penalty, making a CRF of 1.0 attainable.

The maximum CRF is already achieved at injection 7; test one neighboring slope for a slightly shorter run and more margin on its critical pair. The other close pair is expected to remain above 1.5, potentially preserving the maximum score.

The maximum score is already secured; explore a hotter, shallower gradient for greater resolution margin. Higher temperature should further separate the crossed central pair, while the shallower slope may protect its neighboring pair without introducing a time penalty.

With the maximum CRF already secured, test a modestly higher starting organic fraction to assess whether the optimal region extends to another gradient window. The earliest peak remains retained in prior runs, but both close pairs will need monitoring for selectivity changes.

Slightly reduce the slope from injection 10 to recover the newly limiting pair's resolution while retaining the improved separation of the other close pair. This may yield another maximum-score method with all peaks eluting well inside the zero-penalty time window.

Reduce the slope one more grid step to bring the limiting pair above 1.5 while the other close pair is expected to retain adequate resolution. This should preserve zero time penalty and may provide greater minimum-resolution margin than the existing maximum-score methods.

Test a higher starting fraction with a compensating shallower slope to seek more separation margin for both close pairs. Maximum CRF is already secured; this nearby alternative should keep the last peak within the zero-time-penalty window.

Make the gradient slightly shallower than injection 13 to raise the limiting pair above 1.5 while preserving the other close pair's margin. The predicted last-peak time remains below 10 minutes, so this may match the maximum CRF with improved minimum resolution.

A further small slope reduction should balance the two close pairs near resolution 1.7, increasing separation margin while matching the already achieved maximum CRF. The last peak is expected around 9.6 minutes, still within the zero-time-penalty window.

Use a slope between injections 14 and 15 to balance the two critical pairs while targeting another maximum-score run. The trimmed endpoint remains above the estimated last-peak elution fraction of about 0.53, so all compounds should still elute during the gradient.

Refine around injection 12 with a slightly shallower slope and a higher final organic fraction. This should preserve full resolution and zero time penalty while providing a stronger final wash; the maximum achievable CRF is already secured.

Test a slope between injections 11 and 12 to seek a slightly faster maximum-score method with both critical pairs above 1.5. The endpoint remains comfortably above the last peak's estimated elution fraction, minimizing hold-elution risk.

Set the slope between injections 15 and 16 to balance their two limiting pairs near resolution 1.7. This refinement should match the already secured maximum CRF while keeping the last peak below the time-penalty threshold.

Refine the slope between injections 16 and 19 to balance both critical pairs at approximately 1.7 resolution. This untested grid method should retain the maximum CRF with the last peak around 9.4 minutes.

Test a slightly shallower neighbor of injection 17 to characterize the range of methods retaining maximum CRF. Both close pairs are expected to remain above 1.5, with the last peak comfortably below the time-penalty threshold.

Test a slightly steeper neighbor of injection 20 to shorten elution while retaining resolution margin for both critical pairs. The maximum CRF is already secured, and this method is expected to match it with the last peak near 9.1 minutes.

Test a slightly steeper neighbor of injection 22, targeting last-peak elution near 9 minutes while keeping both critical pairs above 1.5. This should extend the confirmed maximum-score region without risking truncation.

Test a trimmed endpoint with a slope close to injection 21, which retained full resolution. The last peak should elute near the gradient-to-hold transition, potentially matching the maximum CRF with a lower final organic fraction.

Use the final injection to test a slightly shallower neighbor of injection 15, targeting full resolution with the last peak just below 10 minutes. The endpoint remains above the observed elution window, and the campaign has already secured the maximum possible CRF of 1.000.
